patch.value:
## Outcome
pm SDK primitives — typed items, custom status graphs, a relationship registry, immutable event history, point-in-time reconstruction, transactional multi-item commits, and bounded graph queries — are sufficient to model domains that have nothing to do with software backlogs.

## Evidence already recorded
Two exemplars landed and closed: a git-like version-control extension and a temporal digital-twin phase-2 exemplar. Their gap reports named the missing primitives; the transaction waiver has since been retired. This milestone tracks the remaining distance.

## Delivery chain
pm-8jdc schema/config completion (incl. pm-z5nb, pm-dijg migrations) -> pm-xc68 policy roles -> pm-is1a federation -> a third foreign-domain exemplar with an empty gap ledger. Depends on the SDK-complete milestone being reached first.

## Explicit non-goals
No domain-specific policy in core. Exemplars are conformance vehicles, not products.
Outcome milestone: universal domain platform — non-PM systems are buildable on pm SDK primitives alone

Custom types, statuses, workflows, fields, and relationship kinds are fully definable at runtime with lossless migration; Principal-based item-level policy is enforced at the SDK layer, not per-surface; Cross-workspace federation supports context, dependencies, and aggregation across many repositories; A published exemplar outside project management ships with an empty SDK gap ledger; Project profiles let a workspace be reshaped for a non-software domain without editing core
A developer models a foreign domain — version control, business workflows, a digital twin — using only public pm SDK primitives
Proves the central product claim: pm is an event-sourced, graph-native context substrate, and project management is one application of it.
Opens the addressable surface beyond software backlogs and turns the extension ecosystem into a platform rather than a plugin list.
At least three foreign-domain exemplars ship with no core forks, no private-core imports, and a published gap ledger that is empty.
The first two exemplars (a git-like VCS and a temporal digital twin) already shipped and produced a gap report; the remaining gaps decide whether the platform claim is real or aspirational.
